_comment: Shared-library SONAME (or library filename stem) -> the component's proper name.
Read by identify-elf-presence.py. A library file in the firmware, or a NEEDED
entry naming one, proves the component is there even when no version string
survives. Stripping 'lib' mechanically does not give the right name —
libnetsnmp.so.30 is net-snmp, not netsnmp — so the mapping is written out.
Rules for adding entries:
- Only add a name you have checked. An unmapped library is reported as
unmapped, which is a smaller error than a wrong name.
- The key is the SONAME with the .so and everything after it removed
(libnetsnmp.so.30 -> libnetsnmp), lowercased.
- No versions. The digits in a SONAME are an ABI number, not the upstream
version: libcrypto.so.1.0.0 is not OpenSSL 1.0.0.
- No purl or CPE either. These judgements carry no version, so they cannot
match a CVE, and attaching an identifier to a versionless component only
invites something downstream to match it against the wrong advisory.
- Runtime pieces of the C library (libpthread, libm, libdl, librt, libutil,
libnsl, libresolv, libcrypt) are deliberately absent: they are the same
component as libc and listing them would report one thing many times.
- libgcc_s and libstdc++ are deliberately absent too. They are GCC's runtime
libraries, and reporting them as 'gcc' would repeat a mistake this corpus
already hit — a compiler marker read as a shipped component.
